newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Surinam recalls ambassador from Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Surinam recalls ambassador from Netherlands.

text.p: Surinam has recalled its ambassador from the Netherlands for a meeting on its relationship with the Dutch government, a spokeswoman for the Surinamese embassy said on Tuesday.
Ambassador Evert Azimullah would leave the Hague on Thursday to travel to the former Dutch colony for a meeting with President Jules Wijdenbosch and Foreign Minister Faried Pierkhan, she said.

The Dutch government's decision to seek the arrest and extradition to the Netherlands of former Surinamese military leader Desi Bouterse for alleged drug smuggling was one of several matters which would be discussed.
"It's more about the relationship of (the Netherlands) and Surinam," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
It was yet to be decided if the ambassador would return to his post, she added.
The Dutch request for police assistance to detain Bouterse has strained already tense diplomatic ties between the two nations.
Surinam last week chastised the Netherlands for seeking the arrest of Bouterse, who staged military coups in the former colony in 1980 and 1990.

Bouterse holds no public office in Surinam, but his National Democratic Party has led a five-party coalition government since elections last year and he was later appointed as an adviser to President Jules Wijdenbosch.
Few observers doubt that he is really controlling government policy from behind the scenes.
Bouterse has long been distrusted by the Netherlands, where many hold him responsible for ordering the summary execution in 1982 of 15 opposition leaders.

Allegations of Bouterse's involvement in drug smuggling have surfaced periodically in the Dutch press, but Dutch authorities confirmed only recently that they were pursuing a criminal investigation against him.
In 1986, a U.S. court gave Bouterse aide Lieutenant Etienne Boerenveen a jail sentence for conspiracy to smuggle cocaine after being arrested by U.S. agents who posed as drug dealers.

Surinam, with a population of just over 400,000, depends heavily on development aid from the Dutch government and has close commercial ties with the country. More than 250,000 Surinamese live in the Netherlands.
